title: One-factor degreewise negative Koszul basis coproduct

from.place: The one-factor base case and the successor induction step split from the recursive degreewise basis coproduct.

statement: For one negative Koszul factor, in each integer degree n the basis maps indexed by subsets I of Fin 1 with n=-|I| form a coproduct of the tensor unit.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, finite free negative Koszul calculation.

proof.text: The recursive length-one complex is the negative two-term factor tensored with the empty tensor O[0]. Use the component of HomologicalComplex.rightUnitor to identify it with the factor. For each supported subset, compute the recursive pure basis map as the factor basis map followed by the inverse right unitor; naturality of the right unitor and equality of the two unitors on the unit prove this normalization.

Every subset of Fin 1 is empty or {0}. The subtype with n=-|I| is therefore a subsingleton. If inhabited, its basis leg is an isomorphism and its inverse defines the coproduct desc; cancellation proves uniqueness. If empty, n is neither -1 nor 0, so the factor is zero in degree n and the right unitor transfers this to the recursive tensor. Zero morphisms give the empty coproduct universal property.

lean.statement:
theorem isColimit_ringedNegativeKoszulBasis_base
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (b : Fin 1 → (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections) (m : ℕ) (n : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk
      ((ringedNegativeKoszul O 1 b m).X n)
      (fun I : {I : Finset (Fin 1) // n = -(I.card : ℤ)} ↦
        ringedNegativeKoszulBasis O 1 b m I.1 n)))
